source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;

records.literal_gloss: Said then the high priest, If these things so are?

en.L: Then the high priest said, "Are these things so?"
en.B: The high priest asked, "Are these charges true?"
en.R: Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Is this true?"

fr.L: Et le grand prêtre dit : « Ces choses sont-elles ainsi ? »
fr.B: Le grand prêtre demanda : « Ces accusations sont-elles fondées ? »
fr.R: Alors le grand prêtre a demandé à Étienne : « Est-ce que c’est vrai ? »

decisions.choice: the high priest: the head of the council before which Stephen stands
decisions.reason: The high priest led the council (5:21, 5:27). Acts does not name him here; Annas and Caiaphas are named among the high priestly family in 4:6.

decisions.choice: are these things so: a direct question whether the charges are true
alternatives: if these things are so (a condition)
decisions.reason: The small word that usually means "if" can introduce a direct question (1:6). "These things" are the charges of 6:13-14, that Stephen spoke against the temple and the law.

decisions.choice: these charges; Stephen
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "these things" are, and Readable names the one asked, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the whole chapter; for Stephen's speech see 7:2.

decisions.choice: le grand prêtre (no hyphen)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form for the high priest in every book; "souverain sacrificateur" is the old Protestant term and now obscure.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.

records.literal_gloss: He then said, Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of the glory appeared to the father of us Abraham being in the Mesopotamia before rather dwelling him in Haran, \v 3 and said to him, Go out from the land of you and from the kindred of you, and come into the land which ever to you I will show.

en.L: And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran, \v 3 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.'
en.B: Stephen replied, "Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran. \v 3 God said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your kin, and come to the land that I will show you.'
en.R: Stephen answered, "Brothers and leaders of our people, listen to me. Long ago the God of glory came and showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Abraham, the father of our nation. At that time Abraham lived in Mesopotamia. He had not yet moved to Haran. \v 3 God said to him, 'Leave your country and your relatives. Go to the land that I will show you.'

fr.L: Et il déclara : « Hommes, frères et pères, écoutez. Le Dieu de gloire est apparu à notre père Abraham quand il était en Mésopotamie, avant qu’il habite à Harân, \v 3 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a dit : “Sors de ton pays et de ta parenté, et viens dans le pays que je te montrerai.”
fr.B: Étienne répondit : « Frères et pères, écoutez. Le Dieu de gloire est apparu à notre père Abraham alors qu’il était encore en Mésopotamie, avant qu’il s’installe à Harân. \v 3 Dieu lui a dit : “Quitte ton pays et ta famille, et va dans le pays que je te montrerai.”
fr.R: Étienne a répondu : « Frères, et vous, les responsables de notre peuple, écoutez-moi. Il y a très longtemps, le Dieu de gloire est venu {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} montrer à Abraham, le père de notre nation. À ce moment-là, Abraham vivait en Mésopotamie. Il n’était pas encore parti s’installer à Harân. \v 3 Dieu lui a dit : “Quitte ton pays et ta famille. Va dans le pays que je vais te montrer.”

decisions.choice: men, brothers and fathers: a formal address to the council, honoring its older members as fathers
alternatives: an address to men and women
decisions.reason: Stephen speaks to the council (6:12, 6:15), whose members were all men, so the address is not widened to men and women, as with Gamaliel's address to the council (5:35). "Fathers" honors the elders and leaders among them; Paul opens his speech to a Jerusalem crowd with "brothers and fathers" (22:1).

decisions.choice: the God of glory: God who shows himself in his glory
alternatives: the glorious God, without the sense of appearing
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Psalm 29:3. The God who "appeared" is the God whose glory is seen, and the speech ends with Stephen seeing the glory of God (7:55).

decisions.choice: Abraham was called while in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran
alternatives: the call came in Haran, as the order of Genesis 11:31-12:4 might suggest
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:31 tells how Terah took Abram from Ur of the Chaldeans to Haran, and the call of Genesis 12:1 is told after that, with Abram leaving Haran (12:4). Stephen places God's appearing before Haran, in Mesopotamia, which 7:4 calls the land of the Chaldeans. Genesis 15:7 and Nehemiah 9:7 say that God brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and Joshua 24:2-3 that God took him from beyond the river. Genesis does not report a call in Ur in so many words. The text is translated as it stands, without settling how the two accounts fit together.

decisions.choice: God's words are Genesis 12:1
alternatives: a summary in Stephen's own words
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 12:1 closely, but leave out "and from your father's house".

decisions.choice: Brothers and fathers
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the formal opening word "men", which English does not use in this kind of address; Literal keeps it. No gender setting applies, since the hearers were all men.

decisions.choice: leaders of our people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom "fathers" honors here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: came and showed himself; the father of our nation
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "appeared" means and in what sense Abraham is "our father".

decisions.choice: Stephen's speech, including his account of Israel's history (7:2-50), in the passé composé at every level, as speech
alternatives: the history (7:2-50) in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps the tenses of speech at every level, including a story told inside a speech, and Stephen is speaking to the council. So his retelling of Israel's history is in the passé composé (with the imparfait and plus-que-parfait where French needs them), as are the retellings in the speeches of Acts 13, 22 and 26. The narrative frame around the speech (7:1-2a, 7:54-60) follows the chapter's narrative rule.

decisions.choice: Harân
decisions.reason: The usual modern French spelling of the town; "Charan" is the older form of Louis Segond.

source.text: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν.

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone out from [the] land of Chaldeans he dwelt in Haran.

en.L: Then, going out from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, he lived in Haran.
en.B: So he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran.
en.R: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and went to live in Haran.

fr.L: Alors, sortant du pays des Chaldéens, il a habité à Harân.
fr.B: Il a donc quitté le pays des Chaldéens et s’est établi à Harân.
fr.R: Alors Abraham a quitté le pays des Chaldéens et il est allé vivre à Harân.

decisions.choice: the land of the Chaldeans: southern Mesopotamia, the region of Ur
decisions.reason: Genesis calls Abram's first home "Ur of the Chaldeans" (Genesis 11:28, 11:31). Haran lay far to the northwest, on the way to Canaan.

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject.

source.text: κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.

records.literal_gloss: And from there after the to die the father of him He removed him into the land this in which you now dwell, \v 5 and not He gave to him an inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and He promised to give to him for a possession it and to the seed of him after him, not being to him a child.

en.L: And from there, after his father died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved him into this land in which you now live. \v 5 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him no inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his seed after him, while he had no child.
en.B: After his father's death, God moved him from there into this land where you now live. \v 5 He gave him no share of it to inherit, not even ground enough for one step. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him and to his descendants after him to hold as their own, while Abraham was still childless.
en.R: After Abraham's father died, God brought Abraham to this land where you live now. \v 5 God did not give him any of the land to own, not even a small piece. But God promised that one day the land would belong to Abraham and to his family after him. God promised this even though Abraham did not have any children yet.

fr.L: Et de là, après que son père est mort, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a fait passer dans ce pays où vous habitez maintenant. \v 5 Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne lui y a donné aucun héritage, pas même [la longueur d’]un pas, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis de le lui donner en possession, ainsi qu’à sa descendance après lui, alors qu’il n’avait pas d’enfant.
fr.B: Après la mort de son père, Dieu l’a fait passer de là dans ce pays où vous habitez aujourd’hui. \v 5 Il ne lui en a donné aucune part en héritage, pas même la place d’un seul pas. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis de le lui donner en propriété, à lui et à sa descendance après lui, alors qu’Abraham n’avait pas encore d’enfant.
fr.R: Après la mort du père d’Abraham, Dieu a conduit Abraham dans ce pays où vous habitez maintenant. \v 5 Dieu ne lui a donné aucune partie de ce pays, pas même un petit morceau de terrain. Mais Dieu a promis qu’un jour le pays appartiendrait à Abraham et à sa famille après lui. Dieu a promis cela alors qu’Abraham n’avait encore aucun enfant.

decisions.choice: Abraham left Haran after his father died
alternatives: Abraham left while his father was still alive
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:26 says Terah was seventy when he fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran; 11:32 says he died in Haran at 205; 12:4 says Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran. Taken together, and if Abram was the firstborn, these would have Terah still alive when Abram left. Genesis tells of Terah's death (11:32) before Abram's leaving (12:4), and Stephen follows that order. The Samaritan Pentateuch gives Terah's age at death in 11:32 as 145, which agrees with Stephen's order. Reviewers should check the Samaritan figure. The text does not explain more, and nothing is added to harmonize it.

decisions.choice: not even the step of a foot: not the smallest piece of ground
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 2:5 in the Greek Old Testament. Abraham later bought a field with a cave to bury Sarah (Genesis 23), but that was a purchase, not land given him to inherit.

decisions.choice: God's promise of the land to Abraham and his descendants
decisions.reason: Genesis 12:7, 13:15 and 17:8 promise the land to Abraham and his offspring; Genesis 17:8 and 48:4 call it a possession. The promise was made while Abraham had no son (Genesis 15:2-3).

decisions.choice: seed: descendants
decisions.reason: The singular word here means Abraham's offspring as a whole, as the next verse shows (7:6).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who moved Abraham; the Greek verb has no stated subject.

decisions.choice: God promised this even though
decisions.reason: Readable makes the closing phrase its own sentence.

decisions.choice: sa descendance (L)
decisions.reason: English Literal keeps "seed", but French "semence" is not used for a person's offspring and would read as agricultural; "descendance" is the plain French word for it (m4), and "postérité" is old-fashioned.

source.text: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·

records.literal_gloss: Spoke however thus the God, that will be the seed of him a sojourner in a land foreign, and they will enslave it and will mistreat years four hundred;

en.L: But God spoke in this way, that his seed would be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they would enslave it and mistreat [it] 400 years.
en.B: This is what God said: his descendants would live as outsiders in a land that belonged to others, and its people would make them slaves and treat them harshly for 400 years.
en.R: God also told Abraham that his family after him would live in a country that was not theirs. The people there would make them slaves and treat them badly for 400 years.

fr.L: Or Dieu a parlé ainsi : sa descendance séjournerait en étrangère dans une terre étrangère, et ils la réduiraient en esclavage et la maltraiteraient quatre cents ans.
fr.B: Voici ce que Dieu a déclaré : sa descendance vivrait en étrangère dans un pays qui appartenait à d’autres, et les gens de ce pays en feraient des esclaves et la maltraiteraient pendant quatre cents ans.
fr.R: Dieu a aussi dit à Abraham que sa famille, après lui, vivrait dans un pays qui n’était pas le sien. Les gens de ce pays feraient d’eux des esclaves et les traiteraient mal pendant quatre cents ans.

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:13, given as reported speech
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:13 closely. Stephen turns them into reported speech, then moves into God's own words in 7:7.

decisions.choice: four hundred years, the figure of Genesis 15:13
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:13 gives 400 years, and Stephen keeps that figure. Exodus 12:40-41 says Israel lived in Egypt 430 years; in the Greek Old Testament and the Samaritan Pentateuch that verse reads "in Egypt and in the land of Canaan". Paul counts 430 years from the promise to the law (Galatians 3:17). The speech quotes the figure of Genesis and does not say how the numbers relate.

decisions.choice: a sojourner: a foreigner living in a land without a citizen's rights
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Moses in Midian (7:29).

decisions.choice: God also told Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the one God spoke to.

decisions.choice: make them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: quatre cents ans
decisions.reason: The English writes the figure; French running text usually writes a round number like this in words, and the Greek writes it as a word.

source.text: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And the nation to which ever they will serve as slaves will judge I, the God said, and after these things they will come out and will serve me in the place this.

en.L: 'And the nation to which they will be slaves I will judge,' God said, 'and after these things they will come out and serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'
en.B: 'But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves,' God said, 'and afterward they will come out and worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'
en.R: God said, 'But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. After that, they will leave that country, and they will worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} here in this place.'

fr.L: “Et la nation dont ils seront esclaves, moi je la jugerai, dit Dieu, et après cela ils sortiront et {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} serviront en ce lieu.”
fr.B: “Mais la nation dont ils seront les esclaves, je la jugerai, dit Dieu, et ensuite ils sortiront et {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendront un culte en ce lieu.”
fr.R: Dieu a dit : “Mais je punirai la nation qui fera d’eux des esclaves. Après cela, ils quitteront ce pays et ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}adoreront ici, dans ce lieu.”

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:14: God will judge the nation that enslaves them
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:14. The plagues on Egypt are that judgment (Exodus 6:6, 12:12).

decisions.choice: worship me in this place: the words of Exodus 3:12, with the place changed
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:14 ends with the people coming out with great possessions. The last words echo Exodus 3:12, where God tells Moses that the people will serve God "on this mountain". Here it is "this place". It may mean the land where Stephen's hearers live (7:4), or the temple, which the charges called "this place" (6:13-14). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: This verb is used of serving God in worship (Luke 2:37, 4:8); the same verb is used in 7:42 of worshiping the stars.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the word that shows this is worship; Literal keeps "serve".

decisions.choice: punish
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's judging the nation would mean for it.

decisions.choice: be slaves / serve as slaves / makes them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

source.text: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to him a covenant of circumcision; and thus he fathered the Isaac and circumcised him on the day the eighth, and Isaac the Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him a covenant of circumcision. And so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac [fathered] Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
en.B: God also gave him the covenant marked by circumcision. And so, when Isaac was born to Abraham, he circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac in turn had Jacob, and Jacob had the twelve patriarchs.
en.R: God made a covenant with Abraham, and circumcision was the mark of it. So when Abraham's son Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him when he was eight days old. Later Isaac had a son named Jacob. Jacob had twelve sons, and they were the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a donné une alliance de circoncision. Et ainsi il a engendré Isaac et l’a circoncis le huitième jour, et Isaac [a engendré] Jacob, et Jacob les douze patriarches.
fr.B: Dieu lui a aussi donné l’alliance marquée par la circoncision. C’est ainsi que, quand Isaac lui est né, Abraham l’a circoncis le huitième jour. Isaac à son tour a eu Jacob, et Jacob a eu les douze patriarches.
fr.R: Dieu a fait une alliance avec Abraham, et la circoncision en était le signe. Alors, quand Isaac, le fils d’Abraham, est né, Abraham l’a circoncis à l’âge de huit jours. Plus tard, Isaac a eu un fils appelé Jacob. Jacob a eu douze fils, et ce sont eux les ancêtres des douze tribus d’Israël.

decisions.choice: the covenant of circumcision: the covenant of Genesis 17, with circumcision as its mark
decisions.reason: In Genesis 17:9-14 God makes circumcision the sign of the covenant between him and Abraham's family.

decisions.choice: and so: under that covenant, Isaac was circumcised
alternatives: and in this way he became a father
decisions.reason: "So" ties Isaac's circumcision to the covenant just named. Genesis 21:4 says Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days old, as God had commanded.

decisions.choice: the twelve patriarchs: the twelve sons of Jacob, from whom the tribes of Israel came
decisions.reason: Genesis 35:22-26 and 49:28 list the twelve sons as the heads of the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver of the covenant.

decisions.choice: twelve sons, the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: l’alliance
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for covenant at every level, Readable included.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the patriarchs having been jealous of the Joseph sold [him] into Egypt; and was the God with him \v 10 and rescued him out of all the afflictions of him and gave to him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruling over Egypt and all the house of him.

en.L: And the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, sold [him] into Egypt. And God was with him, \v 10 and rescued him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his house.
en.B: The patriarchs envied Joseph and sold him off to Egypt. Yet God stood by him \v 10 and delivered him from every hardship he met. He gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who made him governor over Egypt and over all his household.
en.R: Jacob's sons were jealous of their brother Joseph. They sold him, and he was taken to Egypt as a slave. But God was with Joseph. \v 10 God rescued him from all his troubles. God made him wise, and Pharaoh the king of Egypt was pleased with him. Pharaoh made Joseph the ruler over Egypt and over everyone in the king's household.

fr.L: Et les patriarches, jaloux de Joseph, [l’]ont vendu pour l’Égypte. Et Dieu était avec lui, \v 10 et l’a délivré de toutes ses afflictions, et lui a donné faveur et sagesse devant Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, et il l’a établi chef sur l’Égypte et sur toute sa maison.
fr.B: Les patriarches, pleins d’envie envers Joseph, l’ont vendu, et il a été emmené en Égypte. Mais Dieu se tenait à ses côtés \v 10 et l’a tiré de toutes les épreuves qu’il a connues. Il lui a accordé faveur et sagesse aux yeux de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, qui l’a nommé gouverneur de l’Égypte et de toute sa maison.
fr.R: Les fils de Jacob étaient jaloux de leur frère Joseph. Ils l’ont vendu, et il a été emmené en Égypte comme esclave. Mais Dieu était avec Joseph. \v 10 Dieu l’a délivré de tous ses malheurs. Dieu l’a rendu sage, et Pharaon, le roi d’Égypte, l’a apprécié. Pharaon a fait de Joseph le chef de l’Égypte et de tous ceux qui vivaient dans la maison du roi.

decisions.choice: the story of Joseph in Genesis 37-41
decisions.reason: His brothers were jealous of him (Genesis 37:11) and sold him (37:28); God was with him (39:2, 39:21); Pharaoh saw his wisdom and set him over Egypt and his house (41:37-44; see also 45:8).

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes
decisions.reason: The word is the one often translated grace, but here it means favor in the eyes of a person, as in Genesis 39:21, where God gave Joseph favor with the keeper of the prison.

decisions.choice: he appointed him: Pharaoh made Joseph ruler
decisions.reason: The subject changes from God to Pharaoh, as in Genesis 41:41-43.

decisions.choice: the brothers rejected the one God was with
alternatives: a story with no wider point
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers turn against him, yet God is with him and he becomes their rescuer. The speech shows the same pattern in Moses (7:25, 7:35) and comes at last to Jesus (7:52).

decisions.choice: Jacob's sons ... their brother Joseph ... as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were and that Joseph was sold as a slave (Genesis 37:28, 39:1).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... was pleased with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what favor before Pharaoh means, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Came then a famine upon all the Egypt and Canaan and affliction great, and not were finding food the fathers of us.

en.L: Then a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers were not finding food.
en.B: Then famine struck the whole of Egypt and Canaan, bringing great hardship, and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could find nothing to eat.
en.R: Then there was a famine in all of Egypt and Canaan. People suffered terribly. Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could not find any food.

fr.L: Or une famine est survenue sur toute l’Égypte et Canaan, et une grande détresse, et nos pères ne trouvaient pas de nourriture.
fr.B: Puis une famine a frappé toute l’Égypte et Canaan, causant une grande détresse, et nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} ne trouvaient rien à manger.
fr.R: Puis il y a eu une famine dans toute l’Égypte et dans le pays de Canaan. Les gens ont terriblement souffert. Nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} ne trouvaient rien à manger.

decisions.choice: the famine of Genesis 41-42
decisions.reason: Genesis 41:54-57 and 42:5 tell of the famine over Egypt and Canaan.

decisions.choice: food: provisions, anything to live on
decisions.reason: The word was first used of food for animals, but by this time it meant food in general.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here "fathers" means the whole household of Jacob, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then Jacob being grain into Egypt he sent out the fathers of us first;

en.L: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers [the] first [time].
en.B: When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our forefathers there on a first journey.
en.R: Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt. So he sent his sons, our forefathers, to buy some. This was their first trip.

fr.L: Mais Jacob, ayant appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte, a envoyé nos pères une première [fois].
fr.B: Quand Jacob a appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte, il y a envoyé nos pères une première fois.
fr.R: Jacob a appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte. Alors il a envoyé ses fils, nos ancêtres, pour en acheter. C’était leur premier voyage.

decisions.choice: Genesis 42:1-3: Jacob sends his sons for grain
decisions.reason: Jacob sent ten of his sons and kept Benjamin at home (Genesis 42:3-4).

decisions.choice: our fathers: here the sons of Jacob
decisions.reason: The ones Jacob sent to Egypt were his sons, named men (Genesis 42:3), the forefathers of the tribes.

decisions.choice: our forefathers, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Here the word means particular men, the sons of Jacob, so the inclusive setting does not apply; "forefathers" says that plainly.

decisions.choice: his sons ... to buy some
decisions.reason: Readable names those sent and why they went (Genesis 42:2).

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος Ἰωσήφ.

records.literal_gloss: and on the second was made known Joseph to the brothers of him, and known became to the Pharaoh the family of Joseph.

en.L: And on the second [visit] Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh.
en.B: On their second visit Joseph let his brothers know who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
en.R: When they went to Egypt the second time, Joseph told his brothers who he was. And Pharaoh found out about Joseph's family.

fr.L: Et lors de la seconde [visite], Joseph s’est fait reconnaître par ses frères, et la famille de Joseph est devenue connue de Pharaon.
fr.B: Lors de leur second voyage, Joseph a révélé à ses frères qui il était, et Pharaon a été informé de la famille de Joseph.
fr.R: Quand ils sont retournés en Égypte la deuxième fois, Joseph a dit à ses frères qui il était. Et Pharaon a découvert la famille de Joseph.

decisions.choice: Genesis 45: Joseph makes himself known
decisions.reason: Joseph revealed himself to his brothers on their second journey (Genesis 45:1-4), and Pharaoh heard that Joseph's brothers had come (45:16).

decisions.choice: was made known: Joseph made himself known to them
decisions.reason: The passive verb can mean that Joseph let himself be known, as Genesis 45:1 says.

decisions.choice: their second visit
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "on the second"; Balanced and Readable supply the journey meant.

source.text: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε, καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον.

records.literal_gloss: Having sent then Joseph called for Jacob the father of him and all the kindred in souls seventy-five; \v 15 and went down Jacob into Egypt.

en.L: Then Joseph sent and summoned Jacob his father and all [his] relatives, seventy-five souls in all. \v 15 And Jacob went down into Egypt.
en.B: Joseph sent for his father Jacob and for all his relatives, seventy-five people in all, \v 15 and Jacob went down to Egypt.
en.R: Joseph sent a message to his father Jacob. He asked him to come to Egypt with the whole family. There were seventy-five of them. \v 15 So Jacob went down to Egypt.

fr.L: Alors Joseph a envoyé chercher Jacob son père et toute [sa] parenté, soixante-quinze âmes. \v 15 Et Jacob est descendu en Égypte.
fr.B: Joseph a fait venir son père Jacob et toute sa parenté, soixante-quinze personnes en tout, \v 15 et Jacob est descendu en Égypte.
fr.R: Joseph a envoyé un message à son père Jacob. Il lui a demandé de venir en Égypte avec toute la famille. Ils étaient soixante-quinze. \v 15 Alors Jacob est descendu en Égypte.

decisions.choice: seventy-five persons, the number in the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: seventy, the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text gives the number of Jacob's family who came to Egypt as seventy (Genesis 46:27; Exodus 1:5; Deuteronomy 10:22). The Greek Old Testament gives seventy-five in Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5, counting more of Joseph's descendants (Greek Genesis 46:20). A Hebrew manuscript of Exodus from Qumran also reads seventy-five in Exodus 1:5. Stephen gives the number found in the Greek. The counts also differ in whom they include: Genesis 46:26 gives sixty-six. Reviewers should check the Qumran reading.

decisions.choice: in souls: persons, people
decisions.reason: "Souls" here simply counts people, as in 2:41.

decisions.choice: Genesis 45:9-11 and 46:1-7
decisions.reason: Joseph sent for his father, and Jacob went down to Egypt with all his family.

decisions.choice: sent a message ... asked him to come to Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says what Joseph's sending meant.

source.text: καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ.

records.literal_gloss: and died he and the fathers of us, \v 16 and they were carried over to Shechem and were placed in the tomb which bought Abraham for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

en.L: And he died, he and our fathers, \v 16 and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
en.B: There he died, and so did our forefathers. \v 16 They were carried back to Shechem and laid in the tomb Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor at Shechem.
en.R: Jacob died there. Our forefathers, his sons, died there too. \v 16 Later they were carried back to Shechem. They were buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem. He had paid for it with silver.

fr.L: Et il est mort, lui et nos pères, \v 16 et ils ont été transportés à Sichem et déposés dans le tombeau qu’Abraham avait acheté à prix d’argent aux fils de Hamor à Sichem.
fr.B: Il y est mort, et nos pères aussi. \v 16 Ils ont été ramenés à Sichem et déposés dans le tombeau qu’Abraham avait acheté pour une somme d’argent aux fils de Hamor, à Sichem.
fr.R: Jacob est mort là-bas. Nos ancêtres, ses fils, y sont morts aussi. \v 16 Plus tard, on les a ramenés à Sichem. On les a enterrés dans le tombeau qu’Abraham avait acheté aux fils de Hamor, à Sichem. Il l’avait payé en argent.

decisions.choice: the tomb at Shechem: Stephen's account, as it stands
alternatives: Stephen's account adjusted to agree with Genesis and Joshua
decisions.reason: Genesis 23 tells how Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah at Hebron from Ephron the Hittite, and Jacob was buried there (Genesis 49:29-32, 50:13). Jacob bought a piece of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor (Genesis 33:19), and Joseph's bones were buried there (Joshua 24:32). Abraham built an altar at Shechem (Genesis 12:6-7), but no purchase by him there is recorded. The Old Testament does not say where Joseph's brothers were buried. Stephen's words join Abraham's purchase with the place and sellers of Jacob's. The text gives no explanation, and this translation renders it as it stands.

decisions.choice: they were carried: our fathers, and perhaps Jacob with them
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It may take in Jacob as well as the fathers; Genesis 50:13 says Jacob was buried at Hebron. Literal and Balanced keep "they" open.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the sons of Hamor in Shechem"
alternatives: "the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "Hamor the father of Shechem", as in Genesis 33:19; others have "of Shechem". Several early manuscripts have "in Shechem". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: our forefathers, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: These are Jacob's sons, particular men, so the inclusive setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: his sons ... Later
decisions.reason: Readable says who the fathers were and that the burial came later.

source.text: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.

records.literal_gloss: As now was drawing near the time of the promise which had declared the God to the Abraham, grew the people and multiplied in Egypt \v 18 until which arose king another over Egypt who not knew the Joseph.

en.L: And as the time of the promise which God had declared to Abraham was drawing near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, \v 18 until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
en.B: The time was coming close for the promise God had pledged to Abraham, and the people grew and multiplied in Egypt \v 18 until another king rose to rule Egypt, a king who knew nothing of Joseph.
en.R: The time came near for God to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised Abraham. By then the number of our people in Egypt had grown larger and larger. \v 18 Then a new king began to rule Egypt. He did not know anything about Joseph.

fr.L: Et comme approchait le temps de la promesse que Dieu avait déclarée à Abraham, le peuple s’est accru et s’est multiplié en Égypte, \v 18 jusqu’au jour où s’est levé sur l’Égypte un autre roi, qui ne connaissait pas Joseph.
fr.B: Le temps de la promesse que Dieu avait faite à Abraham approchait, et le peuple a grandi et s’est multiplié en Égypte, \v 18 jusqu’au jour où un autre roi est monté sur le trône d’Égypte, un roi qui ignorait tout de Joseph.
fr.R: Le moment approchait où Dieu allait faire ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis à Abraham. Notre peuple, en Égypte, était devenu de plus en plus nombreux. \v 18 Puis un nouveau roi a commencé à régner sur l’Égypte. Il ne savait rien de Joseph.

decisions.choice: Exodus 1:7-8
decisions.reason: The people grew and multiplied (Exodus 1:7). The words of 7:18 follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 1:8 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: the time of the promise: the time for God to keep what he promised Abraham
alternatives: the time the promise was first made
decisions.reason: The promise is the one of 7:5-7, that Abraham's descendants would come out and worship God, and have the land.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "had declared"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "had sworn"; some early manuscripts have "had promised". The sense is close. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: did not know Joseph: knew nothing of him, or cared nothing for what he had done
decisions.reason: The new king had no regard for Joseph and what he had done for Egypt, and so none for his people (Exodus 1:9-10).

decisions.choice: the time came near for God to do what he had promised
alternatives: the time of the promise was drawing near
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the time of the promise" means, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζῳογονεῖσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: This one having dealt craftily with the race of us mistreated the fathers [of us] to make the infants exposed of them unto the not to be kept alive.

en.L: This one dealt craftily with our race and mistreated our fathers, making them expose their infants so that they would not be kept alive.
en.B: He schemed against our people and treated our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} cruelly. He made them put their babies out to die.
en.R: This king tricked our people and was cruel to them. He made our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} leave their babies outside so that they would die.

fr.L: Celui-ci, usant de ruse envers notre peuple, a maltraité nos pères, au point de leur faire exposer leurs nourrissons pour qu’ils ne restent pas en vie.
fr.B: Il a tramé des ruses contre notre peuple et a traité durement nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Il les a forcés à abandonner leurs bébés pour qu’ils meurent.
fr.R: Ce roi a trompé notre peuple et il a été cruel avec lui. Il a obligé nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} à laisser leurs bébés dehors pour qu’ils meurent.

decisions.choice: Exodus 1:10-22
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 1:10 Pharaoh says "let us deal craftily with them", the same verb as here. He ordered the Hebrew boys to be killed (Exodus 1:16, 1:22).

decisions.choice: expose: leave a baby out in the open to die
decisions.reason: Leaving unwanted babies out to die was known in the ancient world. Exodus 1:22 has Pharaoh order every newborn boy thrown into the Nile.

decisions.choice: making them: Pharaoh forced the parents
alternatives: with the result that they exposed their babies
decisions.reason: The construction can express purpose or result. Either way, it was Pharaoh's cruelty that brought it about.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people of Israel in Egypt, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: notre peuple (L)
decisions.reason: English Literal says "race"; French "race" now carries a sense the Greek word for a people descended from one family does not have, so Literal too says "peuple".

source.text: ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·

records.literal_gloss: In which time was born Moses, and was beautiful to the God; who was brought up months three in the house of the father.

en.L: At this time Moses was born, and he was beautiful to God. He was brought up three months in [his] father's house.
en.B: That was the time when Moses was born, and he was a beautiful child before God. For three months he was cared for in his father's house.
en.R: Moses was born at this time. God saw that he was a beautiful baby. For three months his parents took care of him at home.

fr.L: En ce temps-là est né Moïse, et il était beau pour Dieu. Il a été nourri trois mois dans la maison [de son] père.
fr.B: C’est à cette époque qu’est né Moïse, et c’était un bel enfant devant Dieu. Pendant trois mois, il a été élevé dans la maison de son père.
fr.R: C’est à cette époque que Moïse est né. Dieu a vu que c’était un beau bébé. Pendant trois mois, ses parents se sont occupés de lui à la maison.

decisions.choice: beautiful to God: beautiful in God's sight
alternatives: exceedingly beautiful, with "to God" as a way of saying "very"
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:2 says the child was fine; Hebrews 11:23 uses the same adjective. "To God" may mean in God's sight, or it may simply be an emphatic "very", as Jonah 3:3 calls Nineveh a city great "to God". Literal and Balanced keep both open; Readable follows the first.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:2: hidden for three months
decisions.reason: His mother hid him for three months before she could hide him no longer.

decisions.choice: his parents ... at home
decisions.reason: Readable says who cared for him; Exodus 2:2 speaks of his mother.

source.text: ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having been put out then him took up him the daughter of Pharaoh and brought up him for herself as a son.

en.L: And when he was put out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up for herself as a son.
en.B: When he was put outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.
en.R: Then he was left outside. But Pharaoh's daughter took him home and raised him as her own son.

fr.L: Et quand il a été exposé, la fille de Pharaon l’a recueilli et l’a élevé pour elle comme un fils.
fr.B: Quand il a été abandonné dehors, la fille de Pharaon l’a recueilli et l’a élevé comme son propre fils.
fr.R: Puis on l’a laissé dehors. Mais la fille de Pharaon l’a emmené chez elle et elle l’a élevé comme son propre fils.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:3-10
decisions.reason: His mother put him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter found him, and he became her son (Exodus 2:10).

decisions.choice: took up: took him in as her own
decisions.reason: The verb was used of taking up a baby who had been exposed and adopting it, and "as a son" points the same way.

decisions.choice: put out: the same word as "expose" in 7:19
decisions.reason: Stephen uses the word of the king's cruel order. Exodus 2:3 shows Moses's mother placing him in a basket by the river.

source.text: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And was instructed Moses in all wisdom of Egyptians, was then mighty in words and deeds of him.

en.L: And Moses was instructed in all [the] wisdom of [the] Egyptians, and he was mighty in his words and deeds.
en.B: Moses was schooled in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he had power in what he said and in what he did.
en.R: Moses was taught everything the wise men of Egypt knew. He was a powerful man in the things he said and in the things he did.

fr.L: Et Moïse a été instruit dans toute la sagesse des Égyptiens, et il était puissant dans ses paroles et ses œuvres.
fr.B: Moïse a été formé à toute la sagesse des Égyptiens, et il était puissant par ce qu’il disait et par ce qu’il faisait.
fr.R: Moïse a appris tout ce que savaient les sages d’Égypte. C’était un homme puissant, dans ce qu’il disait et dans ce qu’il faisait.

decisions.choice: Moses's training and power: beyond what Exodus records
decisions.reason: Exodus does not tell of Moses's schooling, though as the son of Pharaoh's daughter he grew up at the court (Exodus 2:10). In Exodus 4:10 Moses says he is not a man of words. Stephen says he was mighty in words and deeds; the speech does not say how this fits with Exodus 4:10, and nothing is added to harmonize them.

decisions.choice: mighty in words and deeds: as Jesus was
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same words of Jesus (Luke 24:19).

decisions.choice: everything the wise men of Egypt knew
alternatives: all the wisdom of the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wisdom of Egypt was: the learning of its teachers.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταετὴς χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: When then was being fulfilled to him of forty years a time, it came up upon the heart of him to visit the brothers of him the sons of Israel.

en.L: And when a time of forty years was being fulfilled for him, it came up into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
en.B: As he reached the age of forty, he set his heart on visiting his own kin, the people of Israel.
en.R: When Moses was about forty years old, he decided to go and see his own people, the Israelites. He wanted to see how they were doing.

fr.L: Et quand s’accomplissait pour lui un temps de quarante ans, il lui est monté au cœur de visiter ses frères, les fils d’Israël.
fr.B: Comme il atteignait l’âge de quarante ans, il a eu à cœur d’aller voir les siens, le peuple d’Israël.
fr.R: Quand Moïse avait environ quarante ans, il a décidé d’aller voir son peuple, les Israélites. Il voulait savoir comment ils allaient.

decisions.choice: forty years old: Stephen's figure, not given in Exodus
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:11 says only "when Moses had grown up". Exodus 7:7 makes him eighty when he spoke to Pharaoh, and Deuteronomy 34:7 says he died at 120. Stephen's account divides Moses's life into three periods of forty years (7:23, 7:30, 7:36). The text does not say where the first figure comes from.

decisions.choice: it came up into his heart: he made up his mind
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying that a thought came to someone (Jeremiah 3:16; 1 Corinthians 2:9).

decisions.choice: visit: go to see, with care for them
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking after those in need (15:36; James 1:27), and of God visiting his people to help them (Luke 1:68).

decisions.choice: his own kin, the people of Israel; his own people, the Israelites
alternatives: his brothers, the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: "Brothers" and "sons of Israel" here mean his fellow Israelites, men and women; Balanced and Readable use inclusive words for them; Literal keeps the Greek ones.

decisions.choice: He wanted to see how they were doing
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the visit was out of care for them, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen a certain one being wronged he defended [him] and did vengeance for the one being oppressed having struck the Egyptian.

en.L: And seeing one [of them] being wronged, he defended [him] and took vengeance for the one being oppressed, striking down the Egyptian.
en.B: Seeing one of them being wronged, he stepped in to defend him. He struck down the Egyptian and so avenged the man who was being abused.
en.R: He saw an Egyptian hurting one of the Israelites. So Moses helped the Israelite. He killed the Egyptian to pay him back for hurting the man.

fr.L: Et voyant l’un [d’eux] subir une injustice, il a pris sa défense et a vengé celui qui était accablé, en frappant l’Égyptien.
fr.B: Voyant l’un d’eux maltraité, il est intervenu pour le défendre. Il a abattu l’Égyptien et a ainsi vengé l’homme qu’on brutalisait.
fr.R: Il a vu un Égyptien qui faisait du mal à un Israélite. Alors Moïse a aidé l’Israélite. Il a tué l’Égyptien pour le punir d’avoir fait du mal à cet homme.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:11-12
decisions.reason: Moses saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his kin, and killed the Egyptian.

decisions.choice: struck down: killed
decisions.reason: 7:28 says that Moses killed the Egyptian, as Exodus 2:12 does.

decisions.choice: an Egyptian hurting one of the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names who was wronged and by whom, as the end of the verse shows.

source.text: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.

records.literal_gloss: He was supposing then to understand the brothers that the God through [the] hand of him is giving salvation to them; they but not understood.

en.L: And he supposed [his] brothers understood that God through his hand was giving them salvation, but they did not understand.
en.B: He supposed his kin would grasp that God was bringing them salvation through his hand, but they did not grasp it.
en.R: Moses thought his people would understand that God was using him to save them. But they did not understand.

fr.L: Or il pensait que [ses] frères comprendraient que Dieu, par sa main, leur donnait le salut ; mais eux n’ont pas compris.
fr.B: Il pensait que les siens comprendraient que Dieu leur apportait le salut par sa main, mais ils ne l’ont pas compris.
fr.R: Moïse pensait que son peuple comprendrait que Dieu se servait de lui pour le sauver. Mais ils n’ont pas compris.

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue from slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: Here the word means deliverance from oppression, as in the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 14:13. Stephen's hearers would also hear the word the apostles used of Jesus (4:12).

decisions.choice: through his hand: by means of him, as God's agent
decisions.reason: God is the one giving salvation; Moses is the one God works through (7:35).

decisions.choice: they did not understand: Israel failed to see whom God had sent
decisions.reason: This is Stephen's comment; Exodus does not say it. It fits the pattern of the speech: Joseph was rejected by his brothers (7:9), Moses by his people (7:35, 7:39), and Jesus by his (7:52). Peter speaks of the people acting in ignorance (3:17).

decisions.choice: his kin; his people
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means his fellow Israelites, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

source.text: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών· Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ἐστε· ἱνατί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;

records.literal_gloss: On the and following day he appeared to them fighting and was reconciling them into peace having said, Men, brothers you are; why do you wrong one another?

en.L: And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them to peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers. Why do you wrong one another?'
en.B: On the following day he came upon some of them as they fought, and he tried to bring them back to peace: 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you wronging each other?'
en.R: The next day Moses saw two Israelites fighting. He tried to get them to stop and be at peace. He said, 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you hurting each other?'

fr.L: Et le jour suivant, il s’est montré à eux alors qu’ils se battaient, et il cherchait à les réconcilier en vue de la paix, en disant : “Hommes, vous êtes frères ; pourquoi vous faites-vous du tort l’un à l’autre ?”
fr.B: Le lendemain, il est tombé sur certains d’entre eux qui se battaient, et il a voulu les ramener à la paix : “Mes amis, vous êtes frères. Pourquoi vous faites-vous du tort l’un à l’autre ?”
fr.R: Le lendemain, Moïse a vu deux Israélites qui se battaient. Il a essayé de les arrêter et de les réconcilier. Il leur a dit : “Mes amis, vous êtes frères. Pourquoi est-ce que vous vous faites du mal ?”

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:13
decisions.reason: The next day Moses found two Hebrew men fighting and asked the one in the wrong why he was striking his fellow.

decisions.choice: was reconciling: tried to reconcile
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense here describes an attempt that did not succeed, as 7:27 shows.

decisions.choice: men, you are brothers: two men who belong to the same people
decisions.reason: Exodus 2:13 speaks of two Hebrew men. "Brothers" means fellow Israelites. No inclusive wording applies, since particular men are meant.

decisions.choice: two Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable says who was fighting, as Exodus 2:13 does.

decisions.choice: Mes amis (B, R); Hommes (L)
decisions.reason: English Balanced and Readable keep "Men" as the address, but "Hommes" used to call out to two men sounds odd in French, and "Messieurs" too formal for a quarrel; "Mes amis" is how a French speaker steps between two men fighting. Literal keeps the Greek word.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφ’ ἡμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: The one but wronging the neighbor pushed away him having said, Who you appointed ruler and judge over us?

en.L: But the one wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
en.B: But the one who was abusing his neighbor thrust Moses away and said, 'Who put you in charge as ruler and judge over us?
en.R: But the man who was hurting the other man pushed Moses away. He said, 'Who made you our leader and judge?

fr.L: Mais celui qui faisait du tort à son prochain l’a repoussé, en disant : “Qui t’a établi chef et juge au-dessus de nous ?
fr.B: Mais celui qui maltraitait son prochain a repoussé Moïse et lui a dit : “Qui t’a institué notre chef et notre juge ?
fr.R: Mais l’homme qui faisait du mal à l’autre a repoussé Moïse. Il a dit : “Qui t’a choisi pour être notre chef et notre juge ?

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:14
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 2:14 word for word, and run on into 7:28.

decisions.choice: ruler: one with authority to lead and settle disputes
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 7:35, where God sends Moses as ruler.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses, since two other men are in view.

source.text: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;

records.literal_gloss: Not to kill me you want the way you killed yesterday the Egyptian?

en.L: You do not want to kill me in the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday, do you?'
en.B: Do you mean to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
en.R: Do you want to kill me too, the way you killed that Egyptian yesterday?'

fr.L: Tu ne veux tout de même pas me tuer, toi, de la manière dont tu as tué hier l’Égyptien ?”
fr.B: As-tu l’intention de me tuer comme tu as tué l’Égyptien hier ?”
fr.R: Est-ce que tu veux me tuer moi aussi, comme tu as tué cet Égyptien hier ?”

decisions.choice: a scornful question
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect the answer no, but in this setting it is a taunt: the man knows what Moses did.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:14 continued
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 2:14. Moses then knew that the killing was known.

source.text: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.

records.literal_gloss: Fled then Moses at the word this, and became a sojourner in [the] land of Midian, where he fathered sons two.

en.L: And Moses fled at this word, and became a sojourner in [the] land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
en.B: At these words Moses fled, and he lived as a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he had two sons.
en.R: Because of what the man said, Moses ran away. He went to live in the land of Midian as a foreigner. There he had two sons.

fr.L: Et Moïse s’est enfui à cette parole, et il est devenu un résident étranger dans le pays de Madian, où il a engendré deux fils.
fr.B: À ces mots, Moïse a pris la fuite, et il a vécu en étranger au pays de Madian, où il a eu deux fils.
fr.R: À cause de ce que l’homme avait dit, Moïse s’est enfui. Il est allé vivre comme étranger dans le pays de Madian. Là, il a eu deux fils.

decisions.choice: Exodus 2:15-22 and 18:3-4
decisions.reason: Moses fled from Pharaoh to Midian, married Zipporah, and had two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living in a land not his own
decisions.reason: The same word as in 7:6, where Abraham's descendants live in a foreign land. Moses named his son Gershom, saying he had been a sojourner in a foreign land (Exodus 2:22).

decisions.choice: Midian: the land of the Midianites, in the desert lands south and east of Canaan
decisions.reason: The Midianites were a desert people descended from Abraham through Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2). The bounds of their land are not certain.

source.text: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου·

records.literal_gloss: And having been fulfilled years forty appeared to him in the wilderness of the mountain Sinai an angel in a flame of fire of a bush.

en.L: And when forty years had been fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire of a bush.
en.B: When forty more years had gone by, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire within a bush.
en.R: Forty years went by. Then one day Moses was in the desert near Mount Sinai. An angel appeared to him there in the flames of a bush that was on fire.

fr.L: Et quarante ans s’étant accomplis, un ange lui est apparu dans le désert du mont Sinaï, dans la flamme de feu d’un buisson.
fr.B: Quand quarante autres années se sont écoulées, un ange lui est apparu dans le désert du mont Sinaï, dans la flamme d’un buisson en feu.
fr.R: Quarante ans ont passé. Puis un jour, Moïse était dans le désert, près du mont Sinaï. Un ange lui est apparu là, dans les flammes d’un buisson qui était en feu.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:1-2, with the mountain called Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus 3:1 calls the mountain Horeb. The Old Testament uses both names for the mountain of God: Sinai in Exodus 19:11, Horeb in Deuteronomy 4:10 and 5:2.

decisions.choice: an angel: the angel of the Lord, through whom God himself spoke
alternatives: an angel acting on his own
decisions.reason: Exodus 3:2 says the angel of the LORD appeared in the flame, and then God speaks from the bush (3:4). Stephen too has the voice of the Lord speak (7:31).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "an angel"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "of the Lord", as in Exodus 3:2. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: forty years: the second forty years of Moses's life
decisions.reason: With 7:23 and 7:36, this divides Moses's 120 years (Deuteronomy 34:7) into three forties; Exodus 7:7 gives his age as eighty when he spoke to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: forty more years
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that these forty years follow the first forty of 7:23.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν τὸ ὅραμα.

records.literal_gloss: The and Moses having seen marveled at the sight;

en.L: And when Moses saw [it], he marveled at the sight.
en.B: Moses was amazed when he saw this sight.
en.R: Moses was amazed at what he saw.

fr.L: Et Moïse, voyant [cela], s’est étonné du spectacle.
fr.B: Moïse a été stupéfait en voyant ce spectacle.
fr.R: Moïse a été très étonné par ce qu’il voyait.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:3
decisions.reason: Moses turned aside to see why the bush was not burned up.

decisions.choice: the sight: something seen with the eyes
decisions.reason: The word is often used of visions (10:3, 16:9), but here it is the burning bush that Moses saw.

source.text: προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ κυρίου·

records.literal_gloss: approaching then him to look came [the] voice of [the] Lord:

en.L: And as he was coming near to look closely, there came [the] voice of [the] Lord:
en.B: As he went closer to look, the voice of the Lord came to him:
en.R: He went closer to look at it. Then he heard the voice of the Lord, saying,

fr.L: Et comme il s’approchait pour regarder attentivement, il y a eu la voix du Seigneur :
fr.B: Comme il s’approchait pour regarder, la voix du Seigneur lui est parvenue :
fr.R: Il s’est approché pour mieux regarder. Alors il a entendu la voix du Seigneur, qui disait :

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:4: God calls from the bush
decisions.reason: When the LORD saw that Moses turned aside to look, God called to him from the bush.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew of Exodus 3
decisions.reason: The Greek has the word for Lord. In Exodus 3:4 the Hebrew has the divine name. The voice is God's own (7:32).

decisions.choice: came to him; saying
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add the words English needs to lead into the speech.

source.text: Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ.

records.literal_gloss: I the God of the fathers of you, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.

en.L: 'I [am] the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.'
en.B: 'I am the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.'
en.R: 'I am the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.'

fr.L: “Moi, [je suis] le Dieu de tes pères, le Dieu d’Abraham et d’Isaac et de Jacob.”
fr.B: “Je suis le Dieu de tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob.”
fr.R: “Je suis le Dieu de tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Je suis le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob.”

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6
decisions.reason: God names himself as the God of Moses's fathers (Exodus 3:6, 3:15). Stephen gives these words before the command of Exodus 3:5 (7:33). Jesus quotes the same words in Luke 20:37.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means forebears, as in 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

source.text: ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Trembling then having become Moses not dared to look.

en.L: And becoming terrified, Moses did not dare to look.
en.B: Moses was seized with trembling and did not dare to look.
en.R: Moses was shaking with fear. He was too afraid to look.

fr.L: Et devenu tout tremblant, Moïse n’osait pas regarder.
fr.B: Saisi de tremblement, Moïse n’a pas osé regarder.
fr.R: Moïse tremblait de peur. Il avait trop peur pour regarder.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6: Moses hid his face
decisions.reason: Exodus says Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου, ὁ γὰρ τόπος ἐφ’ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: Said then to him the Lord, Loose the sandal of the feet of you, the for place on which you stand ground holy is.

en.L: Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.
en.B: The Lord said to him, 'Take the sandals off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.
en.R: The Lord said to him, 'Take off your sandals. The place where you are standing is holy ground.

fr.L: Alors le Seigneur lui a dit : “Défais les sandales de tes pieds, car le lieu sur lequel tu te tiens est une terre sainte.
fr.B: Le Seigneur lui a dit : “Retire les sandales de tes pieds, car l’endroit où tu te tiens est une terre sainte.
fr.R: Le Seigneur lui a dit : “Enlève tes sandales. L’endroit où tu es debout est une terre sainte.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:5
decisions.reason: The same command is given to Joshua (Joshua 5:15). In Exodus the Hebrew has the divine name in 3:4 and 3:7; the Greek here has "Lord".

decisions.choice: taking off the sandals: an act of reverence in a holy place
decisions.reason: Removing the sandals showed respect for God's presence (Joshua 5:15).

decisions.choice: holy ground, far from the land and the temple
decisions.reason: Stephen was charged with speaking against "the holy place" (6:13). Here a place in the desert outside the land is called holy, because God is present there.

source.text: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα, καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς· καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen I saw the mistreatment of the people of me the in Egypt, and the groaning of them I heard, and I came down to rescue them; and now come, I will send you into Egypt.

en.L: I have surely seen the mistreatment of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. And now come, I will send you to Egypt.'
en.B: I have seen, yes, seen the cruelty done to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in Egypt. I have heard them groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Come now: I will send you to Egypt.'
en.R: I have seen how badly {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are being treated in Egypt. I have heard them crying out. I have come down to rescue them. So come now. I am sending you to Egypt.'

fr.L: J’ai bien vu l’oppression de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple qui est en Égypte, et j’ai entendu son gémissement, et je suis descendu pour les délivrer. Et maintenant, viens, je t’enverrai en Égypte.”
fr.B: J’ai vu, oui, j’ai vu la cruauté dont souffre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je l’ai entendu gémir, et je suis descendu pour le délivrer. Viens maintenant : je vais t’envoyer en Égypte.”
fr.R: J’ai vu comme on maltraite {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple en Égypte. Je l’ai entendu crier. Je suis descendu pour le délivrer. Alors viens maintenant. Je t’envoie en Égypte.”

decisions.choice: seeing I saw: I have surely seen
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of stressing a verb, carried into the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 3:7.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:7-8 and 3:10
decisions.reason: God has seen his people's suffering, heard their cry, and come down to deliver them, and he sends Moses to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: I have come down: God acts in the world
decisions.reason: The Old Testament speaks of God coming down to see or to act (Genesis 11:5, 18:21).

decisions.choice: I have seen, yes, seen
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress of the doubled verb by repeating it.

source.text: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν, ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν, τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: This the Moses, whom they denied having said, Who you appointed ruler and judge? this one the God both ruler and redeemer has sent with [the] hand of [the] angel the having appeared to him in the bush.

en.L: This Moses, whom they disowned, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?', this one God has sent as both ruler and redeemer, with [the] hand of [the] angel who appeared to him in the bush.
en.B: This was the Moses they had pushed away with the words 'Who made you ruler and judge?' God sent this very man to be both ruler and redeemer, with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
en.R: The Israelites had turned away from Moses. They had said to him, 'Who made you our leader and judge?' But God sent this same Moses to be their leader and to set them free. God sent him with the help of the angel that Moses saw in the bush.

fr.L: Ce Moïse, qu’ils avaient renié en disant : “Qui t’a établi chef et juge ?”, c’est lui que Dieu a envoyé comme chef et libérateur, par la main de l’ange qui lui était apparu dans le buisson.
fr.B: Ce Moïse qu’ils avaient repoussé en disant : “Qui t’a institué chef et juge ?”, c’est cet homme-là que Dieu a envoyé pour être chef et libérateur, avec l’aide de l’ange qui lui était apparu dans le buisson.
fr.R: Les Israélites avaient rejeté Moïse. Ils lui avaient dit : “Qui t’a choisi pour être notre chef et notre juge ?” Mais c’est ce même Moïse que Dieu a envoyé pour être leur chef et pour les libérer. Dieu l’a envoyé avec l’aide de l’ange que Moïse avait vu dans le buisson.

decisions.choice: disowned: refused to accept him
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 3:13-14 of the people disowning Jesus before Pilate.

decisions.choice: the one they rejected is the one God sent
decisions.reason: "This Moses ... this one" is repeated through 7:35-38. Peter spoke the same way of Jesus: the one they rejected God made Lord and Messiah (2:36, 4:11). The speech does not draw the line in so many words until 7:52.

decisions.choice: redeemer: one who sets free
decisions.reason: In Exodus 6:6 God says he will redeem Israel from Egypt. The disciples on the road to Emmaus had hoped Jesus would redeem Israel (Luke 24:21).

decisions.choice: with the hand of the angel: with the angel's help
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means help or agency.

decisions.choice: to be their leader and to set them free
decisions.reason: Readable says what "ruler" and "redeemer" mean here.

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names those who turned Moses away.

decisions.choice: libérateur
decisions.reason: "Rédempteur" is now almost only a theological title of Christ; the Greek word names one who sets free (m3), which "libérateur" says plainly while still pointing to God's act.

source.text: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: This one led out them having done wonders and signs in [the] land of Egypt and in [the] Red Sea and in the wilderness years forty.

en.L: This one led them out, doing wonders and signs in [the] land of Egypt and at [the] Red Sea and in the wilderness forty years.
en.B: It was he who brought them out, working wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
en.R: Moses led the people out of Egypt. He did wonders and signs to show God's power. He did them in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and during the forty years in the desert.

fr.L: Celui-ci les a fait sortir, en faisant des prodiges et des signes dans le pays d’Égypte, et à la mer Rouge, et dans le désert pendant quarante ans.
fr.B: C’est lui qui les a fait sortir, en accomplissant des prodiges et des signes au pays d’Égypte, à la mer Rouge et dans le désert pendant quarante ans.
fr.R: Moïse a fait sortir le peuple d’Égypte. Il a fait des choses extraordinaires et des signes pour montrer la puissance de Dieu. Il les a faits en Égypte, à la mer Rouge et pendant les quarante ans dans le désert.

decisions.choice: the plagues, the crossing of the sea, and the years in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Exodus 7-14 tells of the signs in Egypt and at the sea; Numbers 14:33-34 of the forty years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: wonders and signs: acts of power that show God at work
decisions.reason: The same pair is used of Jesus (2:22), of the apostles (2:43, 5:12), and of Stephen himself (6:8).

decisions.choice: the Red Sea: the name the Greek Old Testament gives the sea Israel crossed
alternatives: the sea now called the Red Sea, with certainty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls it the Sea of Reeds (Exodus 13:18, 15:4). Just which body of water it was is not certain.

decisions.choice: to show God's power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wonders and signs were for, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ.

records.literal_gloss: This is the Moses the having said to the sons of Israel, A prophet for you will raise up the God out from the brothers of you like me.

en.L: This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet from your brothers, like me.'
en.B: This is the Moses who told the people of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people.'
en.R: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, 'God will send you a prophet like me. He will come from your own people.'

fr.L: C’est ce Moïse qui a dit aux fils d’Israël : “Dieu vous suscitera d’entre vos frères un prophète comme moi.”
fr.B: C’est ce Moïse qui a dit au peuple d’Israël : “Dieu vous suscitera un prophète comme moi, issu de votre propre peuple.”
fr.R: C’est le même Moïse qui a dit aux Israélites : “Dieu vous enverra un prophète comme moi. Il viendra de votre propre peuple.”

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 18:15: the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: Peter quoted the same promise of Jesus (3:22).

decisions.choice: the prophet like Moses is Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter applies the promise to Jesus (3:22-26). Stephen sets it here, between Moses rejected and the people's idolatry.

decisions.choice: your brothers: your own people, Israel
decisions.reason: The prophet would be an Israelite, as in 3:22.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "like me"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "him you shall hear", from Deuteronomy 18:15. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel, the Israelites; your own people
alternatives: the sons of Israel; your brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrases mean, as in 3:22; Literal keeps the Greek words.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐδέξατο λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ἡμῖν, ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον, εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών· Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν· ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: This is the one having been in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel the speaking to him in the mountain Sinai and the fathers of us, who received oracles living to give to us, \v 39 to whom not were willing obedient to become the fathers of us, but pushed away and turned in the hearts of them to Egypt, \v 40 having said to the Aaron, Make for us gods who will go before us; the for Moses this, who led out us from [the] land of Egypt, not we know what happened to him.

en.L: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; he received living oracles to give to us. \v 39 Our fathers were not willing to become obedient to him, but they pushed [him] away and turned back in their hearts to Egypt, \v 40 saying to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will go before us; for this Moses who led us out of [the] land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
en.B: He was there in the assembly in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai and with our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, and he received living words to pass on to us. \v 39 Yet our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} would not submit to him. They thrust him aside, and their hearts went back to Egypt. \v 40 'Make us gods to lead the way for us,' they told Aaron. 'This Moses who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him.'
en.R: Moses was with the assembly of God's people in the desert. The angel spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and Moses was there with our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. Moses received words from God that give life, and he passed them on to us. \v 39 But our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} would not obey Moses. They turned away from him. In their hearts they wanted to go back to Egypt. \v 40 They said to Aaron, 'Make us gods to lead us. This Moses brought us out of Egypt, but we do not know what has happened to him.'

fr.L: C’est lui qui a été dans l’assemblée au désert avec l’ange qui lui parlait sur le mont Sinaï, et avec nos pères ; il a reçu des oracles vivants pour nous les donner. \v 39 Nos pères n’ont pas voulu lui obéir, mais [l’]ont repoussé et se sont tournés dans leurs cœurs vers l’Égypte, \v 40 en disant à Aaron : “Fais-nous des dieux qui marcheront devant nous ; car ce Moïse qui nous a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, nous ne savons pas ce qui lui est arrivé.”
fr.B: C’est lui qui s’est tenu dans l’assemblée au désert, avec l’ange qui lui parlait sur le mont Sinaï et avec nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, et il a reçu des paroles vivantes pour nous les transmettre. \v 39 Mais nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} ont refusé de se soumettre à lui. Ils l’ont rejeté, et leur cœur est retourné vers l’Égypte. \v 40 “Fais-nous des dieux qui marchent devant nous, ont-ils dit à Aaron. Ce Moïse qui nous a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, nous ne savons pas ce qu’il est devenu.”
fr.R: Moïse était avec l’assemblée du peuple de Dieu dans le désert. L’ange lui a parlé sur le mont Sinaï, et Moïse était là avec nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Moïse a reçu de Dieu des paroles qui donnent la vie, et il nous les a transmises. \v 39 Mais nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} n’ont pas voulu obéir à Moïse. Ils se sont détournés de lui. Dans leur cœur, ils voulaient retourner en Égypte. \v 40 Ils ont dit à Aaron : “Fais-nous des dieux pour nous guider. Ce Moïse nous a fait sortir d’Égypte, mais nous ne savons pas ce qui lui est arrivé.”

decisions.choice: assembly: Israel gathered as God's people in the wilderness
alternatives: the church of believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the church (5:11), but here it means Israel gathered before God at Sinai. The Greek Old Testament uses it for "the day of the assembly" when the law was given (Deuteronomy 4:10, 9:10, 18:16).

decisions.choice: the angel who spoke at Sinai
decisions.reason: Exodus tells of God speaking to Moses on the mountain. Other passages speak of angels at the giving of the law: Deuteronomy 33:2 in the Greek Old Testament, Galatians 3:19, Hebrews 2:2, and Stephen himself in 7:53.

decisions.choice: living oracles: words from God that are alive and give life
alternatives: oracles that are still in force
decisions.reason: "Oracles" are words spoken by God (Romans 3:2). The law gave life to those who kept it (Leviticus 18:5; Deuteronomy 32:47).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to give to us"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "to you". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Numbers 14:3-4 and Exodus 32:1, 32:23
decisions.reason: The people wanted to go back to Egypt (Numbers 14:3-4). Their words to Aaron follow the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 32:1 and 32:23 closely.

decisions.choice: turned back in their hearts to Egypt: longed to return to Egypt
decisions.reason: They did not go back, but they wanted to (Numbers 11:5, 14:3).

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the people of Israel in the wilderness, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: living words; words from God that give life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plainer words for "oracles", as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: l’assemblée
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "Église" for the church; here the word means Israel gathered in the wilderness (m1), so French uses the ordinary word, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ, καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
